title: Specific heat capacity and latent heat; Entropy and the second law; Electric charge and charging; Coulomb's law
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: T09-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; T09-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; T09-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; T09-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: F01-1#N.2, F02-1#N.4, T02-1#N.3b, T09-1#N.2b, F01-1#N.4b, F02-1#N.8b, T02-1#N.10, T09-1#N.8b, F01-1#N.7, F02-1#N.10, T09-1#N.10, F01-1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Isolated system
items.clue: One whose boundary is crossed by no matter and no energy.

items.label: Entropy
items.clue: Symbol S, unit J K⁻¹: describes how spread out the energy of a system is.

items.label: Reversible process
items.clue: Ideal limit of a change in which total S stays constant instead of rising.

items.label: State function
items.clue: Quantity that depends only on current P, V and T, not on the route taken to reach them.

questions.stem: A small plastic bead has a net charge of −4.8 × 10⁻¹⁷ C. Which statement correctly describes the bead? Use e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

options.text: It has 3.0 × 10² fewer electrons than protons.
It has 3.0 × 10² more electrons than protons.
It has 3.0 × 10² electrons and no protons at all.
It has 4.8 × 10⁻¹⁷ more electrons than protons.

questions.stem: Two small charged spheres whose centres are 0.60 m apart exert electric forces of magnitude 1.0 N on each other. Their charges do not change. At what centre-to-centre separation would the forces have a magnitude of 9.0 N?

An electric kettle heats 250 g of water from 18 °C to 90 °C. The specific heat of water is 4.18 × 10³ J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹. How much energy is transferred to the water? Ignore energy transferred to the kettle and surroundings.
A moving car brakes to a stop. Treat the car, its brakes, the road and the air as an isolated system. Which statement correctly compares the system after the car stops with the system before?

options.text: The total energy is less, because some was used up in stopping the car.
The total energy is the same, but less of it is available to do work.
The total energy is the same, and all of it is still available to do work.
The total entropy is the same, because the total energy is the same.

questions.stem: In an experiment like Millikan's, a student measures the net charge q on each of five oil drops. The bar chart shows the results. Which claim about electric charge do these data support?

options.text: Each is a whole-number multiple of 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
Each result is one reading of a single charge, 7.0 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
The charges follow no pattern, so charge can take any value.
Each charge is a whole-number multiple of 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

questions.stem: Three small charged spheres are fixed on the x-axis: a sphere with charge +q at x = 0, a sphere with charge −4q at x = d, and a sphere with charge +2q at x = 2d. Each can be modeled as a point charge. Which expression gives the magnitude of the net electric force exerted on the +2q sphere by the other two spheres? (k = 1/(4πε₀).)

options.text: 8.50kq²/d²
8.00kq²/d²
6.00kq²/d²
7.50kq²/d²

questions.stem: 0.20 kg of water and 0.20 kg of cooking oil, both at 20 °C, are each supplied with 12 kJ of energy. Specific heat capacities: water 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, oil 2000 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹. Assume no energy is lost. Which statement about their final temperatures is correct?

options.text: The oil ends at 50 °C and the water at about 34 °C.
The water ends at 50 °C and the oil at about 34 °C.
They end at the same temperature, as each gets 12 kJ.
The oil ends at 30 °C and the water at about 14 °C.

questions.stem: A sealed, insulated box is divided by a partition. One side contains a gas, and the other side is evacuated. The partition is removed, and the gas spreads through the box. At which of the following times is the entropy of the gas greatest?

options.text: Before the partition is removed, while the gas is on one side
While the gas is rushing into the empty side most rapidly
At every time equally, since no energy crosses the walls
After the gas has spread out evenly through all of the box

questions.stem: Predict first. A polythene rod is rubbed with a dry wool cloth and gains a charge of −8.0 nC. Which statement about the cloth after the rubbing is correct?

options.text: Its charge is −8.0 nC, because rubbing charges both surfaces in the same way.
Its charge is +8.0 nC, as the electrons the rod gained came from the cloth.
It is uncharged, because the friction created the charge on the rod alone.
Its charge is +8.0 nC, because protons moved from the rod to the cloth.

questions.stem: Two protons are a distance r apart. What is the ratio F_E/F_g of the magnitude of the electric force between them to the magnitude of the gravitational force between them? Use k = 9.0 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻², ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻², G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m_p = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, and m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.

Two identical samples of ideal gas start in the same state. Sample 1 expands slowly at constant temperature, pushing a piston, until its volume has doubled. Sample 2 is in an insulated container and expands freely into an evacuated region until its volume has doubled; its temperature does not change. How do the entropy changes of the two samples compare?

options.text: Sample 2's is greater, because its expansion is irreversible.
The two are equal, and both are greater than zero.
Sample 1's is greater, because only sample 1 is heated.
Both are zero, because neither sample changes temperature.

questions.stem: A negatively charged rod is held near a neutral metal sphere on an insulating stand, and the sphere is connected to ground by a wire. This time the rod is taken away first, and only then is the wire removed. What is the final charge on the sphere?

options.text: Positive, as electrons flowed away through the wire while the rod was near.
Zero, as electrons flow back through the wire once the rod is gone.
Negative, as charge from the rod passes to the sphere through the air.
Negative, as the wire leaves the sphere with the same sign as the rod.

questions.explanation: The order matters. The wire must be removed while the rod is still near, to trap the charge; here the sphere ends neutral.
